Author: @miksstufftt
Content: When I was little, I’d sleep with my bedroom door open because I was afraid of the dark and we’d leave the bathroom light on in the hallway in case I needed to get up. For years, one of my parents would walk down the hall and check on me in the night. I’d hear the floor boards creaking from their room to mine, then they’d peak in, then they’d go back. We moved out years later and they stopped checking on me. One day when I got older I asked why they did that for so many years. Turns out, they never did that. They thought I was the one walking to their room and peaking in. When we moved we hadn’t seen anything like again. I didn’t believe in ghosts for a long time but that realization shook me to my core. I haven’t had any experiences like that since and I hope to never again. It was honestly so scary to think about how many random things happened in that old house that we just assumed was someone else doing something. My parents and I talked about it and genuinely believe that there was something wrong with the house. Although I haven’t had another experience, I sleep with my door closed now.

Author: @rei6262
Content:
10:29 Even as an emo teen with trust issues, I still slept with my bedroom door open. It would always stay closed otherwise, but weirdly enough, I never felt the need to close it at night before. One night, I was struggling to fall asleep, so I lay face up, thinking a change in position might help. That made me face the door directly (I know, not very feng shui). It was only a fraction of a second, but what I saw (or think I saw) on my door frame that night creeped me out enough to never leave my door open again. It looked kinda like my mom. About the same complexion but slimmer, in a sickly way. It looked dishevelled, with sunken eyes and crazy hair, and a wide, creepy smile full of tiny, pointy teeth. It was wearing an old gown, stained in blood. It was peeking into my room and then... it just wasn't there. I don't remember falling asleep.

How did I manage to capture all that in less than a second and with such poor lighting? I don't know. Has the pass of time and fear altered that memory? Probably. Could it have been a nightmare? Most likely. But that was the night I started to close my door.

Years later, I wake up in the middle of the night to grab a glass of water. I bring my phone with me to use the light so I don't bump into things (I have 0 spatial awareness). My brother does sleep with his door open, even 'til this day. When I pass in front of his door, I see it: my mother leaning over his bed, watching him. In the phone light, she looks like one of those ghastly apparitions from found-footage films or video games. I get jumpscared and she looks at me.

Turns out, she was just checking on my brother. She's a lonely woman and both my younger brother and I have had near-death experiences so I guess checking on us like that might comfort her, especially if she gets intrusive thoughts about our well-being (which we all know how those get at night :/). So chances are that's what I saw, and my morbid and hyper, afraid-of-the-dark teenage brain made the rest up. Or I straight up had a nightmare.

Author: @KeiVC
Content:
Some cultural notes if anyone's interested!
1. The long red banners next to doors are usually blessings for fortune, for one's life to flourish etc especially for welcoming the Chinese New Year. The diamond shaped ones with 福 symbolize luck though some people put it upside down too because it's a form of word play that "luck inversed" = "luck arrives". 
2. The fourth floor is seen as unlucky and sometimes skipped in buildings or used for other purposes besides rooms where people stay because 4 sounds like "death"
3. Marbles and chopsticks: sticking chopsticks in rice upright resembles burning incense and/or that setup is only used in food offerings for the dead so its taboo.

Author: @JaySay
Content:
Omg, this game is _REEEAALLLLLLLY_ creepy! I hate that I *love* how eerie it is...🙃

My family has been involved in ghosts/the paranormal for generations, and even though i've had my share of experiences, I still view everything with a skeptical, rational mindset.
Are there things that can never be explained? Sure, but a LOT can be, and plenty of people online will want to fool others just for the satisfaction of doing so.

This game gives me that sense of dread and fear of the _unknown_ that experiencing a lot with suspected ghosts did to me growing up. They did a fantastic job at giving you that constant sense of unease and never giving you the chance to think that you're "safe."
Even when PT came out, it was the scariest game I experienced, probably ever up until that point tbh, but there was still a sense of "oh, this is just some nightmare scenario or made up sensation to scare the hell out of me." This game gives me the thought/feeling that I am in that abandoned apartment, and I. WANT. OUT...!
No thank you, see ya, have a nice day!👋

Author: @Mjelk_Mjolk
Content: I used to sleep with my door open as a child, cus i was scared of the dark, i would also have my cd player that also had radio and a casette player, on all night, mostly the radio tho, but during christmas id play a christmas casette for the mood. Anyway, the lights in the hallway outside my bedroom door was on so it would light up my room. Also, had alot of issues with nightmares, litterly every night, and i used to have hallusinations that would look more real in the dark. Now i need my bedroom to be fully dark, i still sometimes have hallusinations, as that is just a thing i have, but im used to them so i just ignore them, it gets worse if im stressed, but like.. i know they are not real so they dont bother me, also.. less nightmare issues, still get them, but they are more.. weird now.. or just sad. But like, i dont have alot of genuine fears anymore either so.. yeah, i used to sleep with the door open as a child due to fear of the dark, nightlights did not really help as they only light up a bit of the room and honestly just made it creepier.
